source.title: Recurrent neural networks: vanishing and exploding gradients are not the end of the story

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study reports gradient-based training outcomes in linear recurrent teacher-student tasks, using mean-squared loss rather than the classification-error measure and benchmark settings named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study reports results about recurrent-network optimization, but it does not test any listed version: its teacher-student task uses mean-squared loss, and its realistic-task experiments measure signal propagation at initialization. It does not report CIFAR training classification error, the two-layer ReLU local-minimum experiment, shortcut comparisons, the listed initialization comparisons, learning-rate stability behavior, or the listed batch-normalization speed comparison.
record.test_reason: The study's own results concern recurrent-network parameter sensitivity, connectivity, reparametrization and adaptive optimization. None measures the architecture, behavior and outcome combination specified by V1–V6. Signal propagation at initialization alone does not test learning speed or trainable depth in V4, or accuracy gains and learning-rate tolerance in V6. Replace the record's tests/T2 classification.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that long memory creates parameter sensitivity beyond the usual vanishing/exploding temporal-gradient problem; diagonal recurrence facilitates reparametrization and adaptive learning rates that mitigate it. Learning complex eigenvalue angles remains particularly difficult.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes and trains recurrent networks on a linear teacher-student mean-squared-error task and measures signal propagation at initialization; the claim versions concern classification training, feedforward or convolutional architectures, and specific initialization, shortcut, learning-rate, or normalization comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported optimization outcome varies with recurrent architecture and connectivity; signal propagation varies with recurrent memory timescale ν0 and parameter group.

fits_no_version.finding: LRUs outperform dense linear RNNs on long-memory teacher-student tasks despite fewer parameters; block-diagonal connectivity accounts for the main improvement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Restricting recurrent connectivity to diagonal or small independent blocks can improve Adam optimization of long-memory linear teacher-student tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Dense and complex diagonal recurrent models have similar Hessian spectra at optimality but different eigenvector concentration, enabling more targeted adaptive learning rates in the diagonal model.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Coordinate alignment of recurrent-network curvature can determine how effectively Adam compensates for parameter sensitivity.

fits_no_version.finding: At initialization, longer memory increases cRNN activations and gradients; LRU mechanisms mitigate this except for angle gradients, while Chrono-initialized GRU gradient magnitudes remain controlled.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Recurrent architecture, parametrization and memory timescale govern activation and gradient magnitudes at initialization.

record.problems: The training comparison is a synthetic linear recurrent teacher-student task with mean-squared loss, not classification. The paper reports training losses without cross-validation. Several plotted values are not stated numerically in the text. The realistic-task experiments measure signal propagation at initialization rather than trained task performance.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. The remaining figures and appendix analyses are not extracted because they report further recurrent signal-propagation or Hessian analyses outside the listed claim versions.

untested.parts: All: CIFAR convolutional-network training classification error, including random labels and model-size or training-recipe conditions.
All: spurious local-minimum frequency in two-layer ReLU teacher-student networks and the effect of one or two extra student neurons.
All: depth-dependent training error in plain versus identity-shortcut convolutional networks and the specified initialization exceptions.
All: activation-matched initialization effects on plain-network learning speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian tanh networks and 10,000-layer convolutional training.
All: training trajectories relative to learning-rate stability thresholds, catapult recovery, divergence and sustained edge-of-stability behavior.
All: batch-normalization effects on accuracy gain and learning-rate tolerance, and normalization-free Fixup training comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: All row states are cannot_determine relative to V1–V6 because no row measures a listed version; this does not negate their reported recurrent-network findings. The paper cites original work underlying V4–V6, but those citations and its related mechanisms provide no version-level verdict. Appendix C.1.4's failed angle reparametrization concerns a different intervention from V4's initialization claim.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, and the stated model-size, optimizer, stopping, and regularization conditions.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student local minima and the effect of student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual convolutional networks, shortcuts, and the cited normalization-free residual recipes.
The listed activation-matched initializations, their effect on plain-network learning speed or trainable depth, and 10,000-layer plain convolutional training.
Learning rates relative to stability limits, loss recovery or divergence, and sharpness behavior during full-batch training.
Batch-normalization effects on accuracy speed or learning-rate tolerance in the stated image-classification settings, and Fixup comparisons.

rows.subject: linear RNN
rows.size_stated: hidden dimension 64; 10 times as many parameters as the LRU
rows.operation_detail: Trained to reproduce a random linear recurrent teacher using Adam and cosine annealing for 10k steps.
rows.measure: Training mean-squared loss / teacher behavior reproduction
rows.baseline: LRU trained on the same task
rows.value: The text says the linear RNN struggles as the teacher encodes longer dependencies; plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: The authors report the qualitative comparison in text; no exact loss values are stated there. This is a recurrent MSE teacher-student result, not a classification-error result.
rows.check: Recurrent teacher-student MSE does not measure any listed version. Table 1 additionally specifies an initialization scan between ν0 = 0 and the teacher's ν0; these are selected training outcomes after hyperparameter scans.

rows.subject: LRU
rows.size_stated: hidden dimension 64; 10 times fewer parameters than the linear RNN
rows.operation_detail: Trained to reproduce a random linear recurrent teacher using Adam and cosine annealing for 10k steps.
rows.measure: Training mean-squared loss / teacher behavior reproduction
rows.baseline: linear RNN trained on the same task
rows.value: The text says LRUs significantly outperform linear RNNs when long memories must be learned; plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: The authors report this qualitative comparison in text; no exact loss values are stated there.
rows.check: The reported LRU advantage is supported qualitatively, but it does not measure any listed version. Table 1 specifies teacher-matched ν0 initialization and separately tuned learning rates.

rows.subject: RNN
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the linear recurrent teacher-student task with Adam and cosine annealing for 10k steps.
rows.baseline: block-diagonal RNN, complex diagonal RNN, and LRU comparisons shown in Figure 3.B
rows.value: The text says the RNN-to-LRU performance gap mainly comes from making the weight matrix block diagonal; plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: The text describes the qualitative ablation result; it does not state exact plotted training-loss values.
rows.check: This architecture comparison does not measure a listed version. The value describes the overall ablation conclusion rather than a separate training-loss outcome for the dense RNN.

rows.subject: block diagonal RNN
rows.size_stated: 64 hidden neurons; blocks of size 2 in the interpolation setup
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the linear recurrent teacher-student task with block-diagonal recurrent connectivity.
rows.baseline: linear RNN and LRU comparisons shown in Figure 3.B
rows.value: The text says restricting the recurrent matrix to block diagonal yields the main performance improvement; plotted values are figure only.
rows.note: The authors also state that this change reduces parameter count and slightly reduces expressivity.
rows.check: Block-diagonal connectivity improves recurrent teacher-student optimization, outside V1–V6. Table 2 distinguishes the 64-neuron block-diagonal condition from a separate 128-neuron condition.

rows.subject: complex diagonal RNN
rows.operation_detail: Trained on the linear recurrent teacher-student task with complex diagonal recurrent parameters.
rows.baseline: linear RNN, block-diagonal RNN, and LRU comparisons shown in Figure 3.B
rows.value: Figure only; the text attributes the main performance gap to block-diagonal connectivity and says diagonal networks outperform the fully connected counterpart.
rows.note: The text does not give a separate exact or clearly ordered training-loss outcome for this model in Figure 3.B.
rows.check: No listed version is measured. Table 2 specifies teacher-matched ν0 initialization for the complex diagonal RNN, rather than the initialization scan used for real RNNs.

rows.subject: fully connected linear RNN
rows.operation_detail: Measured the Hessian of the teacher-student loss and its eigenvalue structure.
rows.measure: Hessian eigenvalue spectrum and eigenvector structure
rows.baseline: complex diagonal linear RNN with 4 hidden neurons
rows.value: The spectra are almost the same; top eigenvectors are distributed over many coordinates, and the authors say the large terms make learning with SGD almost impossible.
rows.note: This is a curvature and optimization-structure result, not a training classification-error measurement.
rows.check: An optimal-point Hessian spectrum and eigenvector structure do not establish V5's loss recovery, divergence or sharpness trajectory during training.

rows.subject: complex diagonal linear RNN
rows.operation_detail: Measured the Hessian of the teacher-student loss and its eigenvalue structure.
rows.measure: Hessian eigenvalue spectrum and eigenvector structure
rows.baseline: fully connected linear RNN with 4 hidden neurons
rows.value: The spectra are almost the same; top eigenvectors are concentrated on a few coordinates, which the authors say lets Adam compensate for sensitivity more effectively.
rows.note: This is a curvature and optimizer-structure result, not a training classification-error measurement.
rows.check: The Hessian comparison concerns adaptive optimization under different recurrent parametrizations, outside the listed versions.

rows.subject: complex diagonal RNN (cRNN)
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean squared hidden activations and loss gradients as recurrent memory timescale ν0 varied.

conditions.value: next-token prediction with mean-squared error on BERT embeddings of Wikipedia sentences

rows.measure: Mean squared hidden state and gradient magnitude
rows.baseline: LRU and GRU under the same signal-propagation experiment
rows.value: The text says cRNNs suffer from the curse of memory and recurrent-parameter gradients grow faster than gradients for the rest as ν0 approaches 1; precise values are figure only.
rows.note: These are initialization signal-propagation measurements, not benchmark training-error outcomes.
rows.check: Initialization activation and gradient magnitudes do not measure learning speed or trainable depth. The subject is a four-block deep recurrent model on Wikipedia embeddings, not the synthetic toy network; Appendix D.1 also specifies GLUs and skip connections.

rows.subject: LRU
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean squared hidden activations and loss gradients as recurrent memory timescale ν0 varied.

conditions.value: next-token prediction with mean-squared error on BERT embeddings of Wikipedia sentences

rows.measure: Mean squared hidden state and gradient magnitude
rows.baseline: cRNN and GRU under the same signal-propagation experiment
rows.value: The text says LRUs almost perfectly mitigate forward and backward explosion except for the angle parameter; precise values are figure only.
rows.note: These are initialization signal-propagation measurements, not benchmark training-error outcomes.
rows.check: Initialization signal propagation does not measure a listed version. The subject is a four-block deep recurrent model with GLUs and skip connections, rather than a toy network.

rows.subject: GRU
rows.operation_detail: Measured mean squared hidden activations and loss gradients as recurrent memory timescale ν0 varied.

conditions.value: next-token prediction with mean-squared error on BERT embeddings of Wikipedia sentences

rows.measure: Mean squared hidden state and gradient magnitude
rows.baseline: cRNN and LRU under the same signal-propagation experiment
rows.value: The text says GRU gradient magnitude remains constant across characteristic timescales; precise values are figure only.
rows.note: These are initialization signal-propagation measurements, not benchmark training-error outcomes.
rows.check: Chrono-initialized GRU gradient magnitudes do not establish training speed, accuracy or trainable depth. The subject is a four-block deep recurrent model with GLUs and skip connections, rather than a toy network.
